mainTopic: Why רבי עקיבא needs 'בעל השור נקי' for a slave killed by a שור תם, and who receives payment for a killed woman.
overview: Earlier, רבי עקיבא read 'בעל השור נקי' to mean that the owner of a שור תם that kills an עבד pays nothing. The גמרא asks how that can be needed, since a תם pays only from its own body anyway. רב שמואל בר רב יצחק says the case is one where the owner slaughtered the ox first. The גמרא then shows that case needs no פסוק, so that answer falls. רב אסי suggests the פסוק stops payment from the owner's best property, but רבי זירא disproves this from another ברייתא of רבי עקיבא. רבא explains that because the Torah is stricter with an עבד (always thirty סלעים), we might have made a תם pay, and a ברייתא of רבי עקיבא supports him. A new ברייתא then teaches that payment for a killed woman goes to her heirs. ריש לקיש limits this to כופר, which counts as ראוי. The גמרא starts to challenge him from a ברייתא about a woman who miscarried, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's own challenge turned against him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא's own objection does not knock down his own reading of the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי עקיבא ask himself the same question: a שור תם only pays from its own body! So the owner can just say, 'Take the ox to court and get paid from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the question רבי עקיבא asked רבי אליעזר and points it right back at רבי עקיבא's own explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said the verse teaches that the owner of a שור תם that killed a slave does not pay for the slave. But a שור תם never pays from the owner's pocket, only from the ox's body. Once the ox is stoned it is worth nothing, so there is nothing to collect anyway, and the verse seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: To himself, against his own view
But isn't it so that... (a challenge word)
From its body, meaning from the value of the ox itself
An ox that has not yet shown a habit of goring; its owner pays only from the ox's body

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question the גמרא made up. It is the exact objection רבי עקיבא himself raised against רבי אליעזר, now aimed at רבי עקיבא's own reading.

phrases.english: But let Rabbi Akiva say to himself:
But isn't it itself paid
only from its body?
phrases.notes: 'Its body' means the ox itself: damage done by a שור תם is paid only out of the ox's own value.

phrases.english: Bring it to court and it will pay you!
phrases.notes: The owner can tell the slave's master this. But the ox gets stoned, so there is nothing left to collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי עקיבא's earlier objection against רבי אליעזר back onto רבי עקיבא's own reading of the verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading that 'בעל השור נקי' exempts the owner of a שור תם from paying for a killed slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שור תם pays only from its body, and a stoned ox has no value. So the exemption is obvious, and the verse would be teaching nothing.

steps.title: The verse speaks of an owner who slaughtered the ox first
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק explains that the verse is needed for a case where the owner slaughtered the ox before it was sentenced to stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: this is when the owner rushed and slaughtered the ox first. You might think the slave's master can collect from its meat. The verse teaches that since the ox was going to be put to death, even though it was slaughtered, he does not collect from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק saves רבי עקיבא's reading by finding a case where the ox's body does still have value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner slaughters the ox before the court sentences it to סקילה, the meat is kosher and worth money. So we might have thought the slave's master could collect from it. The verse teaches that because the ox was already a בר קטלא (doomed to death), no payment is taken even from its slaughtered meat.

keyTerms.meaning: When he acted first, before the court ruled
And slaughtered it, in a kosher way
You might have thought...
It teaches us (the verse comes to tell us otherwise)
Doomed to be killed, already set for death

steps.whatToRemember: An ox that is a בר קטלא pays nothing for the slave, even if the owner slaughtered it first and its meat is worth money.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said:
It is where its owner first slaughtered it;
phrases.notes: He slaughtered it before the court sentenced it to stoning, so the meat is still worth something.

phrases.english: You might say: let him be paid from it;
it teaches us,
since it is subject to being killed,
even though he slaughtered it,
he is not paid from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: כְּשֶׁקָּדַם בְּעָלָיו וּשְׁחָטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 1 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the verse is set in a situation where the ox's body does have value.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the slaughtered meat is worth money, the slave's master should be able to collect from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the ox was already a בר קטלא, nothing is collected from it, even after kosher slaughter.

steps.title: Then the same answer works for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if this answer works, why did רבי עקיבא challenge רבי אליעזר at all? רבי אליעזר's reading could also refer to an ox slaughtered first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, for רבי אליעזר too, we can say it is a case where the owner slaughtered the ox first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer just given would also have saved רבי אליעזר's reading. So רבי עקיבא's original objection seems weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר read the verse as exempting the owner of a שור תם from חצי כופר. רבי עקיבא attacked this because a שור תם pays only from its body. Now that we know the verse can speak of a slaughtered ox whose meat has value, the same fix would answer רבי עקיבא's own attack.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is your answer
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, according to Rabbi Eliezer as well,
it is where he first slaughtered it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 2 to question why רבי עקיבא objected to רבי אליעזר in the first place.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's earlier objection against רבי אליעזר's reading of the verse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'slaughtered first' case that saves רבי עקיבא's reading would equally save רבי אליעזר's reading, so the objection was not a real problem.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא hoped for a better explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that רבי אליעזר could have answered this way. רבי עקיבא only asked because he thought רבי אליעזר might have an even better explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But רבי עקיבא thought: maybe he has another reason that is better than this one, and he will tell it to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the point. It explains that רבי עקיבא's question was not meant to disprove רבי אליעזר, but to draw out a better answer from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא grants that the 'slaughtered first' answer would also work for רבי אליעזר. רבי עקיבא asked his question hoping רבי אליעזר had a stronger explanation, and indeed רבי אליעזר went on to give one. So רבי עקיבא's question was a request for a better answer, not a refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, indeed, that is so
Perhaps
Another reason or explanation
That is better, stronger

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the 'slaughtered first' case seems to work for both readings of 'בעל השור נקי'. רבי עקיבא's challenge was really asking רבי אליעזר for a stronger explanation. Steps 6–7 show that this case does not really need a פסוק at all, and step 8 brings a new answer.

phrases.english: Indeed, that is so;

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר: דִּלְמָא אִית לֵיהּ טַעְמָא אַחֲרִינָא
phrases.english: but he thought: perhaps he has another reason
that is better than this one, and he will say it.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי אליעזר. רבי עקיבא hoped to hear his better answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי; וְסָבַר: דִּלְמָא אִית לֵיהּ טַעְמָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the point of Step 3 and explains why רבי עקיבא still asked his question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conceding the point and explaining the purpose of the original question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's objection was meant to disprove רבי אליעזר's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The objection was only meant to draw out a better explanation from רבי אליעזר, and the 'slaughtered first' answer also works for him.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי אליעזר use the 'slaughtered first' answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר did not simply answer רבי עקיבא that the case is one where the owner slaughtered the ox first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר too: let him answer רבי עקיבא that the owner slaughtered the ox first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If the 'slaughtered first' answer works, why didn't רבי אליעזר give it himself instead of using a different case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said רבי אליעזר could have answered this way. Now the גמרא presses: then why did he choose a completely different case, where the ox meant to kill an animal and killed a person? There must be a reason he avoided the 'slaughtered first' answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him answer him
That he slaughtered it first, before the court's verdict

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer too:
let him answer him that he slaughtered it first!
phrases.notes: This is the answer of רב שמואל בר רב יצחק from step 2: the owner slaughtered the ox before it was sentenced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 4's claim that רבי אליעזר could have used the 'slaughtered first' answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's choice of a different case for the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the 'slaughtered first' case works, there was no need for רבי אליעזר to pick a different case.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: only my case needs a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר would say that the 'slaughtered first' case needs no פסוק, because that ox was already subject to death. Only his case, where the ox was never subject to death, needs a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: there, where the ox meant to kill an animal and killed a person, the ox is not subject to death at all. So you might think the owner should pay, and the פסוק is needed to exempt him. But here, the ox was subject to death from the start, so no פסוק is needed, even if the owner slaughtered it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אליעזר. In his case a פסוק is really needed, but in the 'slaughtered first' case it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אליעזר's case the ox is not put to death, so the ox is still around and we might think the owner pays from it. That is why a פסוק is needed. But an ox that killed a person was already headed for death, so even if the owner slaughtered it, obviously he does not pay from it. A פסוק would be wasted on that.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you
Subject to being put to death
It intended to kill the animal
To exclude
From the start

phrases.english: He would say to you: It is specifically there,
where it intended to kill the animal
and killed the person instead,

phrases.aramaic: דְּשׁוֹר לָאו בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא כְּלָל;
phrases.english: since the ox is not subject to being killed at all;
so it could enter your mind to say that he should be liable,
the verse was needed to exclude him;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא בַּר קְטָלָא הֲוָה –
phrases.english: but here, where from the start it was subject to being killed,

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיךְ קְרָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּשַׁחְטֵיהּ.
phrases.english: no verse is needed, even though he slaughtered it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by showing why רבי אליעזר avoided the 'slaughtered first' case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases: one truly needs a פסוק, the other is obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'slaughtered first' case would be a fine use of the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: An ox that was subject to death from the start obviously costs the owner nothing, so no פסוק is needed for it.

steps.title: The same logic undoes the answer for רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that by this logic, רבי עקיבא also should not need a פסוק for the 'slaughtered first' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי עקיבא too, it is certainly so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from step 6 back against רבי עקיבא. If no פסוק is needed for the 'slaughtered first' case, then רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's answer for רבי עקיבא falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 explained that רבי עקיבא needs the פסוק for an ox slaughtered before its verdict. But step 6 just showed that such an ox was subject to death from the start, so no פסוק is needed. That logic is true for רבי עקיבא as well, so we are back to asking why רבי עקיבא needs the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly it is so

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רבי אליעזר. It uses the answer given for רבי אליעזר to knock down the explanation of רבי עקיבא from step 2.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Akiva too,
certainly it is so!
phrases.notes: He means that for רבי עקיבא too, no פסוק should be needed when the ox was slaughtered first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי וַדַּאי הָכִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 6 to undo the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's explanation (step 2) of why רבי עקיבא needs the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ox subject to death from the start obviously costs the owner nothing, so the פסוק cannot be needed for that case, even for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רב אסי: the פסוק prevents paying from the owner's best property
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי, in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, gives a new reason why רבי עקיבא needs the פסוק. Since רבי עקיבא holds that a תם that injures a person pays full damages, we might think it also pays for a killed עבד from the owner's best property. The פסוק "בעל השור נקי" teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אסי said: I heard this from a great man, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. You might think that since רבי עקיבא says even a תם that injured a person pays full damages on the difference, the value of a slave is also paid from the owner's best property. So the Torah wrote, "the owner of the ox shall be clear."
steps.whatsHappening: Since the 'slaughtered first' answer has failed, רב אסי offers a whole new explanation of why רבי עקיבא needs the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that for injuring a person, a תם ox is treated like a מועד and pays full damages. So one might think that for killing an עבד, a תם also pays like a מועד: from the owner's best property, not just from the ox. The פסוק "בעל השור נקי" tells us the owner is free of that payment.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man
An ox that has not yet shown a pattern of goring
On the difference (between the two amounts of damage)
The owner's best-quality property
The payment for a slave killed by the ox
The owner of the ox shall be clear (free of payment)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מִילְּתָא – מִפִּי דְּגַבְרָא רַבָּה שְׁמִיעַ לִי,
phrases.english: This matter I heard from the mouth of a great man,
and who is he? Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina:

phrases.aramaic: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא, הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say: since Rabbi Akiva said
that even an innocuous ox that injured a person
pays full damages on the difference,
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה about an ox and a person who hurt each other.

phrases.english: then the payment for a slave would also be paid from the best property;
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote: "The owner of the ox shall be clear."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:28

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 7 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of what the פסוק comes to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a תם pays full damages for injuring a person, it might also pay for an עבד from the owner's best property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק "בעל השור נקי" frees the owner from paying for the עבד from his best property.

steps.title: רבי זירא: רבי עקיבא himself says a תם pays only from its body
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רב אסי from a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא says a תם pays only from the ox's body, never from the owner's best property. So no פסוק is needed to teach that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב אסי: But didn't רבי עקיבא already break the force of his own fist? As a ברייתא teaches: רבי עקיבא says: You might think he pays from his best property. So the פסוק says, "According to this judgment shall be done to him": he pays from its body and not from his best property!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רב אסי's new explanation using a ברייתא of רבי עקיבא himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי said we might think a תם pays from the owner's best property. But רבי עקיבא already limited his own view: a תם pays only from the ox itself, as learned from "כמשפט הזה יעשה לו". Since that is already known, "בעל השור נקי" cannot be needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: He broke his fist, meaning he limited his own strong statement
It is taught in a ברייתא
You might think
The פסוק teaches
From its body (from the ox itself)

steps.whatToRemember: Every attempt to explain רבי עקיבא's use of "בעל השור נקי" has run into trouble: the 'slaughtered first' answer fell away, and now רב אסי's 'best property' answer is challenged by רבי עקיבא's own ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Asi:
But didn't Rabbi Akiva break his own fist?
phrases.notes: A colorful way of saying רבי עקיבא himself softened his strong rule that a תם is like a מועד.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
You might think he pays from his best property;
therefore the verse says: "According to this judgment shall be done to him":
phrases.notes: שמות 21:31. The word לו can also mean "to it," meaning the ox.

phrases.aramaic: מִגּוּפוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם, וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם מִן הָעֲלִיָּיה!
phrases.english: he pays from its body, and does not pay from the best property!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי וְהָא תַּבְרֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לִגְזִיזֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's explanation in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that "בעל השור נקי" is needed to prevent payment from the owner's best property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא already learns from a different פסוק that a תם pays only from the ox's body, so "בעל השור נקי" is not needed for this.

steps.title: רבא's new reason why the verse is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that without the פסוק we might think that, since the Torah is stricter with an עבד, even a תם that kills an עבד pays from the owner's best property. "בעל השור נקי" teaches that the owner is clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The פסוק is needed. You might have thought: since the Torah is stricter with an עבד than with a free man (a free man worth one סלע gets one סלע, and one worth thirty gets thirty, but an עבד worth one סלע still gets thirty), the payment for an עבד should also come from the owner's best property. So the Torah wrote: "The owner of the ox is clear."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי's answer was just knocked down, so רבא gives a brand-new reason why רבי עקיבא needs the פסוק "בעל השור נקי".
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a free man, the payment matches his real value. For an עבד, the Torah sets a fixed thirty סלעים even if he is worth less, which is stricter. Because of that strictness, we might have thought a תם that kills an עבד pays from the owner's best property. The פסוק teaches that the owner is clear.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed. The פסוק is not extra; it teaches something.
It might have entered your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken first thought.
A coin, the unit used for the payment for a killed person
The owner's best-quality property
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two payments for a free man and for an עבד. For a free man the amount follows his value; for an עבד it is always thirty. That fixed amount is exactly why we might have thought to be stricter with an עבד.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is needed,
for it might enter your mind to say:
since I am stricter with a slave
phrases.notes: "I" is the Torah speaking.

phrases.english: than with a free man,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֶּן חוֹרִין יָפֶה סֶלַע – נוֹתֵן סֶלַע,
phrases.english: for a free man worth one sela, he gives one sela,
worth thirty, he gives thirty,
but a slave worth one sela, he still gives thirty;

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁתַּלַּם נָמֵי דְּמֵי עֶבֶד מִן הָעֲלִיָּיה;
phrases.english: so the payment for a slave should also be paid from the best property;
the Merciful One wrote: "The owner of the ox is clear."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:28

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב אסי's answer, which רבי זירא refuted in step 9, with a new reason the פסוק is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of what the פסוק is needed for
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the Torah is stricter with an עבד (a fixed thirty), one might think even a תם that kills an עבד pays from the owner's best property.
steps.terutzMaskana: "בעל השור נקי" teaches that the owner of a תם is clear from payment for the עבד.

steps.title: A ברייתא that matches רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted in which רבי עקיבא reads "בעל השור נקי" as "clear from payment for an עבד," just as רבא explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches like רבא: "The owner of the ox is clear": רבי עקיבא says, clear from payment for an עבד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's reading of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא himself says the פסוק is about the payment for an עבד. That fits רבא, who said the פסוק's job is to free the owner from paying for an עבד killed by a תם.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with him. This brings support for an אמורא.
Clear, meaning free from paying
The payment for a killed עבד (thirty סלעים)

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with Rava:
"The owner of the ox is clear":
Rabbi Akiva says:
clear from the payment for a slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבא's explanation in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's explanation that the פסוק frees the owner from paying for an עבד
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי עקיבא says "נקי מדמי עבד"

steps.title: Couldn't we learn this from logic?
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא asks: why do we need a פסוק? The owner is liable for both an עבד and a בן חורין. For a בן חורין we split between תם and מועד, so we should split for an עבד too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can't this be learned by logic? He is liable for an עבד and liable for a free man. Just as for a free man you split between a תם and a מועד, so for an עבד let us split between a תם and a מועד!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going: רבי עקיבא challenges the need for the פסוק by offering a simple comparison that seems to give the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a free man killed by an ox, only a מועד's owner pays. A תם's owner pays nothing. Since the owner is liable for both a free man and an עבד, the same split should apply to an עבד. Then the תם's owner would be clear without any פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it a logical argument? This asks why a פסוק is needed if logic gives the rule.
An ox with no history of goring
An ox already warned about, with a known goring pattern
A free person

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical argument?
Since he is liable for a slave
and liable for a free man;
just as when the Torah made him liable for a free man
you distinguished between a tam and a muad,
phrases.notes: Only a מועד's owner pays for a killed free man; a תם's owner does not.

phrases.english: so too when the Torah made him liable for a slave
let us distinguish between a tam and a muad!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 11; רבי עקיבא now questions whether the פסוק is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק "בעל השור נקי" to free a תם's owner from paying for an עבד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simple comparison: the owner is liable for both a free man and an עבד, and for a free man תם and מועד are treated differently, so the same should hold for an עבד without a פסוק.

steps.title: A קל וחומר makes it even stronger
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds a קל וחומר: if for a free man, whose full value is paid, we split between תם and מועד, then surely for an עבד, who gets only thirty, we should split too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, a קל וחומר: If for a free man, where he pays his full value, you split between a תם and a מועד, then for an עבד, where he pays only thirty, isn't it logical that we should split between a תם and a מועד?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא strengthens its challenge with a קל וחומר, still asking why the פסוק is needed. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the payment for an עבד is seen as the lighter case, because it is capped at thirty while a free man is paid his full worth. If even the heavier case (a free man) frees a תם, then surely the lighter case (an עבד) should free a תם too. Notice this is the opposite of רבא's angle, where the עבד's fixed thirty was seen as stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: A logic argument: if the rule applies to the stricter case, it surely applies to the lighter case
His value, what he is worth

steps.confusionAlert: רבא in step 10 called the עבד case stricter, because thirty is paid even if he is worth one סלע. This קל וחומר calls it lighter, because only thirty is paid even if he is worth more. Both are true; each argument looks at a different side.

phrases.english: And furthermore, a kal vachomer:
If a free man,
where he gives his full value,
you distinguished between a tam and a muad;
a slave, where he gives only thirty,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁנַּחְלוֹק בּוֹ בֵּין תָּם לְמוּעָד?
phrases.english: is it not logical that we should distinguish between a tam and a muad?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger logic argument to the challenge in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק "בעל השור נקי"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: a free man's full-value payment still frees a תם, so an עבד's smaller, capped payment should surely free a תם too, without a פסוק.

steps.title: The Torah is stricter with a slave, so the verse is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the קל וחומר. For an עבד, the owner sometimes pays more than the slave is worth (always thirty), so we might have thought a תם owner pays for an עבד. 'בעל השור נקי' teaches he is clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can argue the other way: the Torah is stricter with a slave than with a free man. For a free man worth one sela, the owner pays one sela, and if he is worth thirty, he pays thirty. But for a slave worth only one sela, he still pays thirty. So I might think the owner of a תם is liable for a slave. That is why the verse says 'the owner of the ox is clear': clear from paying for a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his own question from Step 12. He shows that the קל וחומר from Step 13 does not work, so the פסוק is needed after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that a slave is the 'lighter' case, since you pay only thirty for him. רבי עקיבא flips this: for a cheap slave you still pay a full thirty, which is stricter than for a free man. Since the קל וחומר can be argued either way, we need 'בעל השור נקי' to teach that a תם owner is clear of slave payment.

keyTerms.meaning: I am stricter (the Torah speaking)
a coin; a basic unit of value
thirty (the fixed payment for a slave)
I might have thought
the verse comes to teach

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, 'בעל השור נקי' teaches that a תם that kills an עבד pays nothing. A קל וחומר could not teach this, because it can be argued in both directions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof (Step 11) that רבא's explanation of the פסוק matches רבי עקיבא's own words.

phrases.english: No, I am stricter with a slave
phrases.notes: The 'I' here is the Torah speaking, as if saying 'I am stricter.'

phrases.english: than with a free man;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֶּן חוֹרִין יָפֶה סֶלַע – נוֹתֵן סֶלַע,
phrases.english: for a free man worth one sela, he gives one sela,
and if he is worth thirty, he gives thirty;
but for a slave worth one sela, he gives thirty.
So I might think he should be liable.
The verse teaches: 'The owner of the ox is clear':
phrases.notes: שמות 21:28

phrases.english: clear from payment for a slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, מַחְמִירַנִי בְּעֶבֶד יוֹתֵר מִבֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of Step 13 and justifies the פסוק questioned in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר that a slave should be treated like a free man (split between תם and מועד).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The slave case is not simply lighter. The fixed thirty can be more than his value, so the Torah is in a way stricter with a slave, and the קל וחומר can be reversed.

steps.title: Why does the verse about a forewarned ox say 'a man or a woman'?
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: רבי עקיבא asks what 'והמית איש או אשה' (the מועד verse) teaches. A woman was already included in the תם verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And it killed a man or a woman.' רבי עקיבא said: What does this come to teach us? If it is to make the owner liable for a woman just as for a man, that was already said: 'When an ox gores a man or a woman'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא asks why the Torah repeats 'or a woman.' This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'man or woman' appear in the תם verse (21:28) and again in the מועד verse (21:29). Since liability for killing a woman is already known from the first verse, the second mention must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
and it killed a man or a woman
what does this come to teach us?
it was already stated

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And it killed a man or a woman':
phrases.notes: שמות 21:29, the verse about a מועד ox.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
What does this come to teach us?
If it is to make him liable for a woman as for a man,
it was already stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי יִגַּח שׁוֹר אֶת אִישׁ אוֹ אֶת אִשָּׁה״!
phrases.english: 'When an ox gores a man or a woman'!
phrases.notes: שמות 21:28, the verse about a תם ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא of רבי עקיבא about the next verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra lesson the repeated words 'או אשה' in the מועד verse teach.

steps.title: A woman is compared to a man: payment goes to her heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the verse compares a woman to a man. Just as payment for a man goes to his heirs, payment for a woman goes to her heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to compare a woman to a man. Just as for a man, his damages go to his heirs, so too for a woman, her damages go to her heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his answer: the repeated words teach who receives the payment when a woman is killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability itself was already known, so the extra words teach a new point about where the money goes. The money goes to her heirs, just as it would for a man. The next step shows the גמרא understanding this to mean her husband does not get it.

keyTerms.meaning: to compare (two cases placed side by side in a verse)
his damages (the payment for him)
his heirs

phrases.english: Rather, it is to compare a woman to a man:
just as for a man, his damages go to his heirs,
so too for a woman, her damages go to her heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse compares a woman to a man, so payment for a woman's death goes to her heirs.

steps.title: But רבי עקיבא holds that a husband inherits his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רבי עקיבא really hold that a husband does not inherit his wife? A ברייתא records that he learns from 'וירש אותה' that a husband does inherit her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי עקיבא hold that a husband does not inherit his wife? But it was taught: 'And he shall inherit her.' From here we learn that a husband inherits his wife. These are the words of רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two statements of רבי עקיבא. It sets up the need for an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 seemed to say that payment for a woman goes to her heirs and not to her husband. But in another ברייתא, רבי עקיבא himself learns that a husband is his wife's heir. If so, why would the husband not get the payment?

keyTerms.meaning: and does he hold?
inherits
but it was taught in a ברייתא
and he shall inherit her

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Akiva hold
that a husband does not inherit her?
But it was taught:
'And he shall inherit her':
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:11. The word אותה can be read as 'her,' meaning the wife.

phrases.english: from here we learn that a husband inherits his wife;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָא יָרֵית לַהּ בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of Step 16 using another statement of רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's teaching that payment for a woman goes to her heirs (implying not to her husband).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא elsewhere derives from 'וירש אותה' that a husband inherits his wife, so the husband should be her heir and receive the payment.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the husband does not inherit כופר because it counts as 'due'
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says רבי עקיבא excluded the husband only from כופר. Since כופר is paid only after death, it is ראוי (due), and a husband does not inherit ראוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: רבי עקיבא said this only about כופר. Since it is paid only after death, it counts as property that was 'due' to her. A husband does not inherit what was due to his wife the way he inherits what she actually owned.
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ answers the question from Step 17. רבי עקיבא agrees that a husband inherits his wife, but כופר is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband inherits what his wife owned while alive (מוחזק). כופר only comes into being after she dies, so she never owned it. It counts as ראוי, and the husband does not inherit ראוי, so it goes to her other heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom payment the owner of a מועד ox pays when his ox kills a person
Property that was only due to come to someone, not yet actually owned
Property someone actually owned and held
After death
Since, because

steps.confusionAlert: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ is not saying the husband never inherits his wife. He does inherit what she owned. He only loses out on money that first became due after her death.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
He said it only about ransom,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, who said the payment for a woman goes to her heirs (Step 16).

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין מִשְׁתַּלֵּם אֶלָּא לְאַחַר מִיתָה,
phrases.english: since it is paid only after death,
so it counts as property that was 'due',
and the husband does not take what was due the way he takes what she owned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא אָמַר אֶלָּא בְּכוֹפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to one case (כופר), based on the difference between ראוי and מוחזק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רבי עקיבא holds that a husband never inherits his wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband inherits what she owned. כופר is only ראוי, so it goes to her heirs.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a husband does not inherit ראוי the way he inherits מוחזק is a general inheritance principle, used here to make the two statements of רבי עקיבא fit together.

steps.title: Source that כופר is paid only after death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason and quotes the פסוק: the ox is stoned, and then כופר is laid on the owner. Stoning happens only after a death, so כופר does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The verse says: 'And it killed a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death. If a ransom is laid on him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that כופר is paid only after death, and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'and it killed', then 'the ox shall be stoned', and only then mentions כופר. So כופר is linked to an actual death. Even if the victim is clearly about to die, nothing is owed until he dies, which is why it counts as ראוי.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The verse says
Shall be stoned
Is laid upon him

phrases.english: What is the reason? The verse says:
phrases.notes: The question is how we know כופר is paid only after death.

phrases.english: "And it killed a man or a woman,
the ox shall be stoned,
and its owner also shall be put to death.
If a ransom is laid on him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in Step 18 that כופר is paid only after death.
steps.raayaObject: That כופר is owed only after the victim dies
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the פסוק: killing, then stoning, then כופר

steps.title: Doesn't רבי עקיבא say the same about damages?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: does רבי עקיבא really limit this to כופר? It seems he says the same about damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about damages, did רבי עקיבא not say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's limit to כופר. This line sets up a ברייתא that comes next as the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ said רבי עקיבא gives the woman's payment to her heirs only for כופר, because it is ראוי. The גמרא suggests רבי עקיבא gives payments to her heirs, not her husband, in damages (נזקין) too, which would not fit the ראוי reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Damages: payments for injuries to a person or property

phrases.english: And about damages, did Rabbi Akiva not say this?
phrases.notes: He means: doesn't רבי עקיבא also give damages owed to a wife to her heirs, not her husband?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's claim that רבי עקיבא spoke only about כופר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי עקיבא also gives a woman's damages to her heirs, then the reason cannot be that כופר is ראוי.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a woman who was struck and miscarried
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. Someone who strikes a woman and causes a miscarriage pays her for damage and pain, and pays the husband for the babies. If one of them has died, the payment goes to that person's heirs. The ברייתא continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: If someone struck a woman and her babies came out, he gives payment for damage and pain to the woman, and payment for the babies to the husband. If the husband is not alive, he gives it to the husband's heirs. If the woman is not alive, he gives it to her heirs. If she was a maidservant and was freed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its challenge from Step 20. The quote is not finished here; it continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key line is 'if the woman is not alive, he gives it to her heirs'. Her damage payment goes to her heirs, not to her husband. Damages are owed while she is alive, so they are not ראוי, and that seems to go against רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ. The case of a freed maidservant starts a new detail that the next part completes.

Payment for the injury and for the pain
Payment for the lost unborn babies
A non-Jewish maidservant
She was freed

phrases.english: But it was taught: if someone struck the woman
and her babies came out,

phrases.english: he gives payment for damage and pain to the woman,
